### Premise re-verified on `origin/main` this fire, ⛔ not relayed from triage

| premise | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the marker is still authored by the inspector | ✓ `ViewColumnInspector.tsx:279` — ``unknownValueLabel={(v) => `${v} (not in object)`}`` |
| the string is a real i18n key | ✓ `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — `notInObject` present |
| the primitive still has no 「roster has not answered」 term | ✓ — see the correction below |
| ⭐ lit control | `InspectorSelectField` resolves in `_shared.tsx` ⇒ the instrument reads the file |

⚠️ **One reading differs from triage's, and the difference is instructive rather than a defect.** Triage recorded `loading` / `pending` on that component as **0 hits**; this seat measured **1**. Printed, it is `_shared.tsx:330` — a **comment inside `InspectorSelectField`** reading 「closing it needs a **loading contract** this primitive [lacks]」.

⇒ triage's substantive finding is **confirmed**, not weakened: the primitive has no loading term, and the single hit is prose **naming that absence**. ⭐ It also makes the card stronger — the gap is already known and documented at the site. ⛔ Recorded because a bare count cannot tell code from prose, which has now bitten this lane four times in one shift.

### Why `Clause-②: no`

The fix gives `InspectorSelectField` a way to tell 「the roster has not answered」 from 「the value is genuinely not offered」, so the `(not in object)` marker stops firing during an in-flight round trip. That is a **narrowing of a false claim**, ⛔ not a relaxation of anything.

And the component is **not published surface** — measured: `git grep -nw InspectorSelectField` across `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` returns **zero**, with a lit control of **92** `export` lines in that same barrel, and 20 in-package consumers. ⇒ a new prop on it widens no published face.

⚠️ If implementation finds the fix must move a **published** type or an authorable key, that is the fork: **stop and report**, ⛔ do not revise the declaration after the fact.

### ⭐ The judgement this card was dispatched for, made correctly

The card could have been fixed per call site or once at the primitive. It was fixed **once**: `InspectorSelectField` gains `loading`, turning a boolean into a tri-state — roster answered and value offered / roster answered and value absent (flagged, unchanged) / **roster not yet answered (drawn bare, no claim)**. ⭐ The synthesised row still renders in the pending arm, so the trigger never blanks and the value stays re-pickable — **only the assertion is withheld**, which is the narrowest possible fix.

All three of my unverified premises came back resolved, ⛔ not assumed:
- **(a)** every loader named on the card (`useObjectFields`, `useDatasetCatalog`, `useDatasetSemantics`, `useMetaOptions`) **already publishes** a loading signal ⇒ nothing had to be threaded through a hook, which is what made the primitive-level fix cheap.
- **(b)** objectui#8488 **is landed** ⇒ the blast radius is live, and was re-measured rather than copied.
- **(c)** the sibling `(not found)` family shares the **rule** but not the **defect** — those call sites take synchronous rosters or sit behind an `options.length` gate.

⭐ And my corrected reading of the `_shared.tsx:330` comment was confirmed by **printing** it, not counting it — then the comment was replaced by the contract it had been asking for. That is the right way to close a documented gap.

### ⭐⭐ The card's call-site list is CORRECTED, and I verified the correction

The card names `ActionTargetField` as reaching this shape. **It does not.** Re-derived by this seat at source: `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx:219` — `const usePicker = !!metaType && options.length > 0;` — so the select **never mounts** while the roster is empty; a text field renders instead, and there is no marker to withhold. ⇒ threading the prop there would have been dead code.

Fixed where the defect actually reaches: the `ViewColumnInspector` field-key picker, and `ReportDefaultInspector`'s dataset binding plus both chart axes. Everything else is either gated the same way or takes a synchronous roster.

### ⭐ Two suites at two altitudes, and the ablation proves why both exist

The defect only exists **while the request is in flight**, so both suites pin that frame. The asymmetry is the load-bearing part, ⛔ not the redness:

- **LEG A** (ablate the primitive's read) → RED on all five pending-arm rows **and** both end-to-end in-flight rows; GREEN and unchanged on the answered-arm rows and the true negative.
- **LEG B** (ablate **only** `loading={fieldsLoading}` at the call site, primitive untouched) → primitive suite **entirely GREEN**, end-to-end in-flight rows RED.

⇒ leg B is the argument for the second suite's existence: a primitive-only pin cannot see the seam. The end-to-end suite drives the real `useObjectFields` against a metadata client whose promise is **held open**.

⭐⭐ **One measurement changed a test, and the reason is recorded on its own commit.** On the first ablation the end-to-end true negative was reading the **in-flight** frame, so leg A turned it red for the *pending* reason and it stopped being able to testify about the answered one. 「Both legs failing on a single ablation is exactly what a true negative exists to rule out」 ⇒ that case was decoupled and the reported readings are from the re-run. That is a dev noticing its own instrument was compromised and saying so.

1. ⭐ **It corrected its own already-posted GitHub report.** The comment on the card (`5707465871`) carries `+466/−14` in a parenthetical — an estimate written before the final diff was measured. The measured figure is **`+525/−14`**, which the PR confirms. 2. ⭐ **It named a rule conflict instead of silently resolving it**: objectui `AGENTS.md` §9 authorises a **claiming seat** to self-merge once CI is green, while the dispatch forbids merging and forbids awaiting CI. It took the dispatch and said so. ⇒ **for the record, there is no real conflict**: §9 addresses the **claiming seat** — that is this seat, not a dispatched dev — so the dev never held that authorisation to begin with. ⛔ Naming it was still correct; an agent that resolves an apparent rule conflict silently is the failure mode.
3. `Clause-②: no` re-measured this fire rather than inherited: `git grep -nw InspectorSelectField` over `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` → **0**, against a lit control of **92** export lines. No fork reached, nothing revised after the fact.
